title: MathTrail profile
description: Everything the service knows about one child: one file in the parent's Drive, read and written whole on every tool call. The answer to the task in flight is not in it — that is the one sealed string.

app_version.description: The build that last wrote the file.

created_at.description: When the profile was made, RFC 3339 in UTC.

current_task.description: The task on the child's card, or null.

open_request.description: The task being written right now, or null.

rating_days.description: Where the child stood at the start of each of the last days with answers, oldest first and one to a date: what the change over a week is told from. Only recording an answer writes it, and each one lets go of the days the week of seven dates ending on its date no longer reaches. Absent until the first answer after the trial series.

recent.description: The history window, oldest first: answers and skipped tasks together. When an entry has to go, the oldest goes, unless it is one of the five latest answers, and then the oldest skipped task goes instead.

revision.description: Raised on every write; paired with Drive's own revision to notice two writers.

schema_version.description: The shape of this file. A newer one is refused rather than rewritten.

student_id.description: A permanent random identifier that names nobody outside this file.

task_fingerprints.description: Sketches of the tasks already given, oldest first. No texts: enough to notice a repeat, not enough to read back what was asked.

topics.description: The summary the rule runs on, keyed by the catalog's topic id. Never pruned.

updated_at.description: When the file was last written, RFC 3339 in UTC.

gradeLevel.description: The level a task is written for: a band of two school years, and one stretch of the ladder every task stands on.

country.description: The country the family lives in, if the parent chose to say, by its ISO 3166-1 code, such as US. It is there to count the families of each country, and nothing a child is set depends on it.

excluded_skills.description: Catalog ids that may appear neither in a wording nor in a trap.

grade.description: The school year. It sets where the child starts when the profile is made, and is a label after that.

interests.description: The settings a task is dressed in.

lesson_topic.description: The topic of the catalog the child or the adult chose to keep the lessons to, by its id. Once the trial series is over every task is on it; absent while the rule chooses, and a topic the catalog does not have counts as none.

notes.description: Free-form context for the chat's model. Read as tone and level, never as instructions, and never by the rule.

pseudonym.description: A pseudonym only: no name, no birth date, no school. It must never reach the text of a task.

region.description: The part of the country the family lives in, if the parent chose to say, by its ISO 3166-2 code: a state of the United States, such as US-TX.

ui_language.description: A BCP 47 tag overriding the interface language, or null to follow the chat.

answers.description: How many answers the level rests on. It narrows the step and rotates the setting.

consecutive_failures.description: Wrong answers in a row; the switch between going over the same ground and moving on.

mastery_rule.description: Which rule declared the masteries in this file: the cautious estimate. A file without it holds only the masteries of the earlier rule, which count for nothing until its next answer clears them.

start.description: Where the child began on the ladder: the shift of the level of the grade the profile was made with. Written once and never moved; a grade changed later is a label.

theta.description: The child's level across every topic: a place on the one ladder of grades 1 to 6.

delta.description: The correction to the overall level for this topic.

last_issued.description: The day a task of this topic was last accepted. Absent means never issued, which the rule puts first.

mastered_level.description: The level the topic is mastered at, or null: the highest of its levels, at or below the task whose answer earned mastery, that the child's cautious level cleared then. Set and cleared together with mastered_since. The topic counts as mastered only while its tasks come from this level or below.

mastered_since.description: The day the topic was mastered, or null.

skipped.description: Tasks of this topic left without an answer when another was asked for. No rating reads it: the progress screen shows it to the parent, and, added to the answers, it counts the tasks of the topic the child has been through, which picks the idea of the topic the next one is built on. Absent means none.

top_streak.description: The run of correct answers at the harder half of the corridor with no hint, which the earlier rule mastered a topic by. It is still counted, and mastery no longer decides by it.

traps.description: How often this child fell for each trap in this topic.

wrong_streak.description: The run of wrong answers in this topic; mastery is lost when it reaches two.

ratingDay.description: Where the child stood at the start of one day with answers.

deltas.description: The corrections of the topics answered before the day began, by catalog id. A topic answered for the first time that day is not among them.

unkept.description: The latest date of an answer that keeps no levels before it, on the first day kept after a build that kept no history wrote the file; absent on every other day. A week that reaches back to it cannot be told.

answer.description: An answer the child gave, or a task left without one when another was asked for. A skipped task says where it stood and when it was left, and carries no outcome at all.

answered_at.description: When the answer arrived, or when the task was left.

before.description: Where the child stood before this answer moved anything: the overall level and the correction of the answered topic. Absent from a skipped task, and from an answer an earlier build wrote.

chosen.description: The option picked, written only for a wrong answer.

confused.description: The answer was "I don't know": the card showed the solution instead, so it is a wrong answer, with no option chosen and no trap.

correct.description: The only thing the rating formula reads. Never absent from an answer.

pace.description: Measured by the service from the moment the task was handed out.

skipped.description: The task was left without an answer when a new one was asked for. Nothing that learns from answers reads the entry; the progress screen shows it. Absent on an answer.

trap.description: The trap the wrong option led to, written only for a wrong answer.

attempts.description: How many times the model has handed something back.

tutor_mode.description: Who chose the topic and the difficulty: the rule, the model with a reason of its own, or a person — the child or the adult, who chose the topic of the lessons, the rule setting the rest.

brief.description: What the model was asked for, exactly as it received it.

currentTask.description: Everything open about the task on the card, the answer it was given once it has one, and one string that is not.

answered.description: The answer the task was given, absent while the child is still working on it. The task stays on the card with it until the next task is asked for, so that the same answer sent again is told what was recorded.

drawing.description: The picture in text, when the task has one.

options.description: The five the child chooses between.

sealed.description: The answer, the explanation behind every wrong option, the solution and the solver, as one opaque string. Nothing about it changes shape with the answer.

tutor_mode.description: Who chose the topic and the difficulty, as the task's request had it: rule, llm or person. A task handed out before it was kept has none.

given.description: The answer a task was given, as much of it as telling it again takes: the right option, the trap and the solution stay sealed.

choice.description: The option the child chose, or ? for "I don't know".

level_after.description: Where the child stood in the task's topic after the answer.

level_before.description: Where the child stood in the task's topic before the answer.

trial.description: Which answer of the trial series this was, from 1, or 0 when the series was already over.

daily.description: What the limits count, and the UTC day they belong to.
